en: The *Suvarṇamālā-stuti*:
Now, O Lord, somehow I purify my seat with even a mere fragment of Your virtues—O Sāmba, Sadāśiva, Śambhu, Śaṅkara; Your pair of feet is my refuge. (1)
O Ākhaṇḍala, O Expert in shattering the pride [of the Asuras], O Beloved of Taṇḍu, O Lord of Caṇḍī, O All-pervading One! O Sāmba!
O You who wear elephant-hide as a garment, O Enemy of Śambara, O You whose eyes blaze with fire, O All-pervading One! O Sāmba...
O Lord of the Mountain, O Lord of Men, O Supreme Lord, O Great Lord, O Ornament of the Serpent-dweller (Śeṣa), O Blessed One! O Sāmba!
O Lord, whose left side is embraced by Umā, whose form is divinely auspicious...
Sāmba... 5 Accept me, ignorant and protectorless; O Sāmba, remove my misfortune!
6 O Swan of the minds of the best of sages, cause of the origin, sustenance, and dissolution of all that moves and is stationary... Sāmba... 7

O Lord of the Bears, O Diadem-wearer, O All-pervading One who has shaken off the Rudrākṣa beads while mounted upon the Great Bull, [I bow] to You together with Ambā... 8 O All-pervading One, I offer the pair of *lṛ* vowels to Your feet like two beautiful flowers on a single stalk; [I bow] to You together with Ambā...
O Merciful One, O Śambhu... we worship You alone as the "One Being" according to the Vedic scripture which declares, "Thou art indeed Being."
O Viśvaṃbhara, you bestow unity upon your own devotees; here, O Mṛḍa, the Goddess Māyā is our witness that she is your instructor, saying "Om," O benefactor of us who are with Ambā... O Sāmba... 12.
And your nakedness, O Lord, clearly demonstrates your indifference toward sense objects, O [you who are] with Ambā... O Sāmba...
O Lord, O Sāmba, grant me purity of the internal organ and devotion unto you, which is true.
O Lord, you are the embodiment of the universe through all forms—both collective and individual—of the infinite limiting adjuncts; O Amba, [you are] the liberated one...
O Sāmba, abode of the ocean of compassion, it is not fitting for you to be indifferent toward me, your servant.
O Sāmba... break apart association with the wicked and constantly cultivate union with the virtuous alone.
O Lord, you have swallowed the poison for the sake of benefiting the world; who indeed is equal to you here, O Sambhu?
O Lord Sāmba, you whose body is white with thick streams [of ash] and upon whom the Gaṅgā is bound in a mass of abundant matted hair...
19 O Lord Sāmba, you who are consciousness, you shine as the indivisible essence within all bodies...
20 O Lord Sāmba, firmly bind my fickle monkey of a heart, which wanders among the objects of the senses... 21
O Śiva, O Sāmba! Oh, even the shadow of you who stand like a tree-stump removes the sin of those who bow to you!
O Lord who dwells on victorious Kailāsa, Sovereign of the hosts of Pramathas, worshipped by the gods on earth, O Sāmba...!

O Great Dancer, with the sound of the *jhaṇutaka*, *iṅkiṇu*, and *jhaṇutatkiṭataka* ornaments, O Lord Sāmba, grant me knowledge free from distraction and other such hindrances; you alone are my Guru, O All-pervading One, O Sāmba... 25. The sound of the *ṭakka* upon your bow pierces the hearts of enemies like a thunderbolt, O Lord Sāmba... 26.
O Sāmba, your illusory power (māyā) is indeed like a hollow shell, empty in form both within and without.
O Sāmba, your pair of sinless feet even shatters the lotuses of hypocrisy. ... [End of verse]
O Sāmba, O Lord whose hands shine with the ḍhakkā drum, the rosary, the trident, and the skull-bowl!
If Your refuge, which contains the form of Śiva, grants auspiciousness here to men, O Sāmba... 29 O Sāmba...
30 A person who meditates upon You and recites Your mantra crosses the ocean of worldly existence instantly, O Sāmba... 31
O Lord, may the sound of "dhūṭ" arise from the mouth of him who has no name for You; O Sāmba...

॥32॥ Who in this world is more pitiable than I, and who is more compassionate than You? Tell me, O Sāmba, O Teacher of the Three-Eyed One, skilled in establishing the Dharma, O Punisher of Dakṣa’s sacrifice! O Sāmba... ॥34॥
O Lord Sāmba, were you not struck by a bow in the past with a cruel intent by the man Nara? You are unable to be measured; O unborn one, you are higher than the highest, O Lord Sāmba.
O Lord, O All-pervading One, accompanied by Ambā, the fruit of this human birth is the eternal service at Your feet.
O Lord, grant us strength, health, long life, and a lasting delight in your virtues.

O Bhagavān, Bharga, remover of fear, Lord of beings, whose limbs are adorned with ashes, O All-pervading One, [grant us] Sāmba... O Consort of the Daughter of the Snow-Mountain-Holder, your greatness does not fit within the Vedas, O Lord. [Grant us] Sāmba...
O Sāmba... O Lord, the self-controlled ones worship the pure essence within Your heart through the limbs of practice such as the restraints (yama) and observances (niyama).
O All-pervading One, O Sāmba... the worlds appear within You, just as a rope appears as a snake or as silver appears in a mother-of-pearl shell.
O Lord, by Your grace, Cakra protects the entire world;
O Sāmba, [protect] that earth where the Asuras have been vanquished by the arrows of Viṣṇu and the discus!
O Śarva, God supreme over all, giver of everything, O All-pervading One who destroys the pride of the wicked—O Sāmba... 45.
O Destroyer of the six enemies, the six waves, and the six transformations; O Six-faced One, Father, All-pervading Lord, together with Ambā... [sāmba...]

O Lord Sāmba, may that Brahman characterized by the definition "Truth, Knowledge, Infinite" [be] yours... 47 O All-pervading One, whose feet are the source of the verses sung by the celestial singers Hāhā and Hūhū, may there be auspiciousness for you always, O Lord Sāmba... 48 May there never be the use of words beginning with *la* here; rather, let there always be auspiciousness ending in *ma*, O Lord Sāmba... 41
"O Śiva, O Sāmba, eager for the moment of serving your feet, he will pass the days as if they were a mere instant.
Thus [ends] the work of the venerable Śrī Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (paramahaṃsaparivrājakācārya).
The *Suvarṇamālā-stuti* is complete.
